spec.name: Reversal v25
spec.notes: Fade the last move, rebalanced often.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 2.4, annual return 12%, maximum drawdown 6%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.43 to -0.12 (change -2.55).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 2.43 to 2.43. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 1.71 (as submitted, 5 bps: 2.43); it breaks even at 21.5 bps with daily turnover 0.29.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 2.43 against 2.43 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is -1.84 against 2.43 in research, a gap of +4.28.
The best year gives 28% of total P&L (year 1) and calm regimes give 72%; Sharpe is 2.41 in calm and 2.72 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 2 distinct specs; the best of 2 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.00, so the claimed 2.40 becomes 2.40 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 3.13 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.02, 95th percentile 0.57).
Perturbing the 2 numeric values in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.43 to as low as 1.25 (as low as 2.04 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (23 days) give 30% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 22% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first

verdict.opinion: Rejected: core test damaging (lag_test EX-1, holdout_test EX-5).
